text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Public sector sees renewed labour tension as urban transportation workers plan new strike for February 6, and civil servants plan to fight for higher wages.
-- Insurer GAN to present restructuring plan today that may include cutting up to 591 jobs.
-- Paris bourse CAC 40 blue-chip index at record highs, markets expect U.S. Federal Reserve to maintain a monetary status quo on February 4.
-- Coca-Cola fined 10 million francs by French competition council for breaching fair competition rules for the French soft drinks market.
-- Company failures were up nine percent after falling for two years, according to report by reinsurance firm SFAC, a member of Euler group.
-- French bank branches in Hong-Kong optimistic over growth potential in spite of planned handover to China.
-- Housing minister Pierre-Andre Perissol favours an alternative to transferring part of Credit Foncier's activity to Credit Immobilier de France.
-- Spie Batignolles construction group chairman denies a planned leveraged buyout by company's employees is designed to allow Britain's Amec to buy it in turn.
-- Societe Generale chairman Marc Vienot worries French banks are losing their wealth, fears thay may not be strong enough to withstand another crisis.

-- French state's indebtedness reached 3,500 billion francs at the end of 1996, or 45 percent of GDP, up from 30 percent of GDP four years ago. Average maturity of debt falls to six years and 47 days compared to six years and 95 days at end 1995.
-- Success of Robien law allowing tax cuts for firms that reduce work hours to create or save jobs raises criticism over cost of employment subsidizing.
-- Workers in public and semi-public financial institutions such as Banque de France, Caisse des Depots et Consignations, demonstrate to express support to Credit Foncier staff.
